facts.text: Immaculata University was founded in 1920 as Villa Maria College, the first Catholic women’s college in the Philadelphia area.
The Sisters, Servants of the Immaculate Heart of Mary founded the campus, and the university remains part of the larger IHM community that includes a nearby academy for girls.
The campus spans more than 300 acres in Chester County’s Great Valley, growing from the original 198‑acre plot to 373 acres today.
In 1972, the Mighty Macs basketball team won the national championship, a story later made into a film directed by Tim Chambers.
The three‑story Gabriele Library houses a coffee shop called ImmacuLatte, blending study space with a caffeine fix.
In 2005, Immaculata became co‑educational, opening its doors to male students for the first time in its history.
